brief.goal: Show what Sparkade is and how it works: walk up, snap a photo, and the arcade dreams up a game starring you.
brief.audience: Social: YouTube, LinkedIn and X (16:9); TikTok, Reels and Shorts (9:16)
brief.notes: The vertical cut skips the "what if AI…", build, Voice Transcribe, SAM and engines beats so it stays short. Master to −14 LUFS with peaks at or below −1 dBTP. Captions burned in.

material.summary: Kiosk and phone captures, cabinet photos, real game output

structure.summary: Script locked; narration recorded with the Danny clone

sound.summary: Two music beds fitted to the voice; −14 LUFS master

lines.text: This arcade doesn't want your quarters. It wants your face.
Snap a photo, and it dreams up a brand new game, starring you.
I love retro games. Enough to build a whole fleet of arcade cabinets, just to run emulators.
So I started wondering: what if AI could make games nobody has ever played?
I reused my Raspberry Pi mini arcade design, with one small upgrade: a camera and mic, built right into the marquee.
Walk up, snap a photo, and tell it what you want to play.
From there, it's all Meta's Model API, and every model has a job.
Muse Voice Transcribe turns your idea into text.
Muse Spark is the brains. It writes the story, designs the levels, and even composes the music.
Muse Image paints everything you see. Heroes, enemies, bosses, backgrounds.
And I'm testing SAM 3.1 to cut out sprites with pixel perfect masks.
To keep it fast and reliable, the AI never writes code. It tunes one of six game engines I built, each with hundreds of knobs.
While it builds, scan the QR code to follow along on your phone.
About five minutes later, your game is ready. And it typically costs under fifty cents.
Play it right here on the cabinet, or anywhere on your phone.
Platformers. Shooters. Fighters. Racers. Every single one, brand new.
Sparkade. The arcade that dreams up its own games.

shots.label: Insert face
shots.intent: Cabinet turntable. INSERT COIN blinks, a quarter bounces off, and it glitches to INSERT FACE. Your real kiosk selfie in a viewfinder, then a 3‑2‑1 countdown and shutter flash. The photo dissolves pixel by pixel into your Muse‑made hero. STARRING YOU plays over 4 cuts of your games' key art.

shots.label: Logo slam
shots.intent: Music drop. The logo slams in and the tagline types out.

shots.label: Cabinet fleet
shots.intent: Your cabinets (photos and turntable), then hands on the stick.

shots.label: What if AI…
shots.intent: A terminal prompt types the question.

shots.label: Mini arcade build
shots.intent: Pi in the back panel, the CAD model, a 16× build time‑lapse (GoPro footage flipped 180°), then a zoom into the marquee with CAMERA and MIC callouts.

shots.label: Walk up
shots.intent: Real kiosk selfie footage, then the kiosk recording your spoken idea and Muse Voice Transcribe filling in the details.

shots.label: Select your team
shots.intent: "Meta Model API" title with the @AIatMeta launch post, then a SELECT YOUR TEAM character select of the 4 models.

shots.label: Voice Transcribe
shots.intent: Waveform, then the transcript types out. Quote card from @finkd.

shots.label: Muse Spark
shots.intent: The real spec Muse wrote for this game: its story intro, a scrolling tile map of level 1, and a piano roll of its theme. You hear Muse's actual composed chiptune at that moment. Quote card from @finkd.

shots.label: Muse Image
shots.intent: The key art paints in, then the real sprites pop in on each word. Chips read "45 images painted · $0.01 each". The @MetaforDevs quote card is on 16:9 only.

shots.label: SAM 3.1
shots.intent: A real SAM 3.1 run on your pajama‑hero sprite: green screen → mask → clean cutout. @MetaforDevs quote card.

shots.label: Six engines
shots.intent: Code gets a NO CODE stamp, then the 6 engine cards, then a wall of real schema setting names as spinning knobs ("~300 settings per engine").

shots.label: Follow along
shots.intent: The kiosk's "MUSE IS BUILDING" screen with the QR card highlighted. A phone slides in showing sparkade.dev's live "Sparkade is building." page.

shots.label: Game ready
shots.intent: Fast‑forward through the real build log (timer counts to 3:14), then GAME READY! on the chorus downbeat. The price counts up to $0.44 with an UNDER 50¢ stamp.

shots.label: Play anywhere
shots.intent: Hands on the cabinet, then a phone playing on sparkade.dev with the on‑screen touch controls lighting up.

shots.label: Gameplay montage
shots.intent: Real gameplay on each word, then a wall of game art pulls back, then fast beat‑cut gameplay.

shots.label: Tagline
shots.intent: Logo, tagline, a QR to sparkade.dev and the model credits.

shots.label: Burned-in captions
shots.intent: One word at a time, current word in cyan. Off while the title, montage and tag lines are on screen as kinetic type.
